etymologies.etymologyHTML: From scare +‎ -y.

definitions.definition: (now chiefly informal) Causing fear or anxiety

quote.citation: 1884 December 10, Mark Twain [pseudonym; Samuel Langhorne Clemens], chapter 29, in The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn: (Tom Sawyer’s Comrade) […], London: Chatto & Windus, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Well, we swarmed along down the river road, just carrying on like wildcats; and to make it more scary the sky was darking up, and the lightning beginning to wink and flitter, and the wind to shiver amongst the leaves.

quote.citation: 1982, Anne Tyler, chapter 2, in Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant‎[1], New York: Ivy Books, published 1992, page 70:
quote.text: “ […]  How scary it is to know that everyone I love depends on me! I’m afraid I’ll do something wrong.”

quote.citation: 2007 September 2, Terrence Rafferty, “Technicolor Dreamboat”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: Age notwithstanding, none of these men seem interested in sailing to Byzantium anyway: Justine’s got them all on the last stage to someplace wilder and scarier, where Yeats’s “monuments of unaging intellect” are thoroughly beside the point.

quote.citation: 2020, Lesley L. Smith, A Jack For All Seasons, page 45:
quote.text: The biggest, scariest, scarriest man in the room said, “It's about time, Jones.”

definitions.definition: (US, colloquial) Subject to sudden alarm; easily frightened.

quote.citation: 1823, James Fenimore Cooper, chapter 5, in The Pioneers‎[3], volume 2, New York: Charles Wiley, the UK edition of the same year has scary (p. 262)[4], page 77:
quote.text: “Whist! whist!” said Natty, in a low voice, on hearing a slight sound made by Elizabeth, in bending over the side of the canoe, in eager curiosity; “’tis a sceary animal, and it’s a far stroke for a spear.  […] ”

quote.citation: 1867, John Greenleaf Whittier, The Tent on the Beach, and Other Poems‎[5], Boston: Ticknor and Fields, The Wreck of Rivermouth, page 25:
quote.text: “She’s cursed,” said the skipper; “speak her fair:I’m scary always to see her shakeHer wicked head, with its wild gray hair,And nose like a hawk, and eyes like a snake.”

quote.citation: 1916, Texas Department of Agriculture, “Bulletin”, in (Please provide the book title or journal name), numbers 47-57, page 150:
quote.text: And let us say to these interests that, until the Buy-It-Made-In-Texas movement co-operates with the farmers, we are going to be a little scary of the snare.

quote.citation: 1940, Richard Wright, Native Son‎[6], book 1, London: Jonathan Cape, published 1970, page 10:
quote.text: The two brothers stood over the dead rat  […] .“Please, Bigger, take ’im out,” Vera begged.“Aw, don’t be so scary,” Buddy said.

quote.citation: 2010, Peter Corris, Torn Apart, Allen and Unwin, page 117:
quote.text: At 199 centimetres and a hundred kilos going up, he was scary big and he found work as a bouncer and enforcer[.]

quote.citation: 2020, S. Clarence Dodge, Beyond Blood: Inside the Mind of an Anesthesiologist‎[7], Xlibris Corporation:
quote.text: [T]he main reason I don't want to give her a GA is she's so scary fat!

definitions.definition: Barren land having only a thin coat of grass.
